lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Why are you crying, Tantalus? What's all this moaning, standing by a lake?
lines.note: Opening line: Menippus's tone is genuinely curious, not unkind — he finds this baffling rather than distressing.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Because, Menippus, I'm dying of thirst.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Surely you're not so lazy that you can't just bend down and drink — or, good lord, cup your hands?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: It doesn't help. The water runs away the moment it senses me coming. And if I do manage to scoop some up and bring it to my mouth, I've barely wet my lips before it slips through my fingers somehow and my hand is dry again.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Extraordinary situation. [pause] But tell me — what exactly do you need to drink for? You don't have a body. That's buried somewhere in Lydia, and it was the body that could get hungry and thirsty. You're a soul. How would you even drink? What would you do with it?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: That's precisely the punishment. The soul thirsting as if it were a body.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All right, fair enough — I'll take your word for it that the thirst is real. But here's what I'm not following: what's the actual catastrophe? Are you afraid you'll die from lack of water? Because I don't see another underworld on the other side of this one, or a second death to somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: You're not wrong. And I suppose that's part of the sentence too — craving something you don't actually need.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Tantalus, you're talking nonsense. And if you genuinely think you need a drink, what you need — by Zeus — is a strong dose of hellebore. You've got it exactly backwards from those people bitten by rabid dogs: they're afraid of the water. You're afraid of the thirst.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Honestly, Menippus, I wouldn't say no to the hellebore either, if I could only get some.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Cheer up, Tantalus. You won't drink, and neither will anyone else down here. That's simply not how it works. Though I'll grant you this: most of the dead aren't thirsty by court order, with the water making a point of avoiding them specifically.
lines.note: Final line: Menippus delivers this as a mild consolation that isn't one. The closest thing to sympathy he offers — which is still mostly an observation.
